MISC.label: Junk
MISC.summary: Loot dropped by monsters with no use but gold — body parts, hides, feathers, minerals, oddments. Sold at any shop.

SOUL.label: Soul Stone
SOUL.summary: A soul stone dropped by monsters — the card of one specific creature. Merged into a weapon or a piece of armor to grant it the stone's power; the stone is consumed by the merge. `one_per_monster` makes the binding STRICTLY 1-to-1: a stone is dropped by exactly one monster and a monster drops exactly one stone, so the wiki can show the creature on the stone and the stone on the creature. A stone with no monster yet is UNBOUND (it waits for one) — never a second stone on a monster that already has one.

CONSUMABLE.label: Consumable
CONSUMABLE.summary: Used from the bag for an immediate effect — potions, elixirs, food. Consumed on use.

SWORD.label: Sword
SWORD.summary: Melee weapon. Equipped in the weapon slot; can carry merged soul powers.

BOW.label: Bow
BOW.summary: Ranged weapon. Equipped in the weapon slot; can carry merged soul powers.

WAND.label: Wand
WAND.summary: Magic weapon. Equipped in the weapon slot; can carry merged soul powers.

ARMOR.label: Armor
ARMOR.summary: Worn protection. Equipped in the armor slot; can carry merged soul powers.

monsters.name: Ironhide
monsters.lore: Armor that grew instead of being forged. Spears skate off its plates; its tusks do not return the favor.
monsters.loreDesc: Armor that grew instead of being forged. Spears skate off its plates; its tusks do not return the favor.

loreStory.t: Sigrun

calls it a cheat. Everyone laughs, and she is not joking. She has given a working life to the shoulder — the gap a plate harness has to leave so the arm can go up, and therefore the gap everything gets in through. Every smith who ever lived has failed at the shoulder. This animal wears bands that slide across one another when it breathes and shut when it turns, and it earned none of them, and does not know it has them.

loreStory: She has been out to look at one four times now, taking no tools, getting no nearer than she has to, standing there watching a beast breathe — the least Sigrun-like thing she does all year. The tusks curve out low and forward and they are built for lifting; what they lift is whatever was standing in front of it. She has not made a shoulder yet.

Understand what she is actually trying to build. Nothing out here can be ended with a spear, so people take plate for vanity. Sigrun has watched what a bad shoulder really costs: a person goes down, re-forms by the nearest fire some hours later, and comes back short a little of what they were thinking — a face, a stretch of road, a name that gave them no trouble last year. It is not a wound. It is a subtraction, it does not come back, and they turn up at her door afterwards unable to say quite why they came. That thing out on the plain has never lost one thought to a spear in its life. She goes back next week.

monsters.name: Duskhoof
monsters.lore: A black horse that casts no shadow. It stamps, and the dark pools around its hooves like spilled ink.
monsters.loreDesc: A black horse that casts no shadow. It stamps, and the dark pools around its hooves like spilled ink.
loreStory: There is nothing whatever wrong with this horse. Sound feet, good coat, eats, sleeps, comes when it is called, hauls whatever you put behind it and does not sulk about the load. The only thing it does not do is lay a shadow on the ground. On a bright day people will watch the grass beside it for a while, and then find a reason to be somewhere else.

It has had a dozen owners and been handed on a dozen times, and every one of them offered a different reason out loud: too big for the yard, wrong temperament, no work for it this season. The reason none of them offered is that everybody knows which end of a long story a missing detail comes off, and a good horse you are going to have to stand and watch is worse than no horse at all.

loreStory.t: Sigrun

took it four years ago and has not handed it on. It hauls charcoal, stands in the yard behind the smithy while she works, and in the evening she scratches the place under its jaw it likes until it leans its whole considerable weight into her hand. People who know what she has already sat through in her life ask her, carefully, whether that is wise. She says the horse hauls charcoal.

monsters.name: Sporehorn
monsters.lore: The fungus steers the elk now. Its antlers bloom green in the dark, sowing spores wherever it grieves.
monsters.loreDesc: The fungus steers the elk now. Its antlers bloom green in the dark, sowing spores wherever it grieves.

loreStory.t: Sporehorn keeps a circuit.
Gunnar

walked it out over two winters — he maps ground that will not hold still, and an animal that repeats itself was a rest — and got three stops: a ford, a burnt orchard, and a bare slope above the orchard with nothing on it at all. It stands at the ford a while. At the orchard a while. At the bare slope until the light goes.

There was a hut on that slope. Gunnar asked eleven people before he found one who could still say so, and she could not produce the woman's name — only that she kept goats and fed whatever came to the door, elk included. The hut is not there now, nor the track up to it. Things nobody tells about
go soft, and then go
, and that elk is the last thing in the world that still turns up.

loreStory: The fungus did not pick the route. It has only worked out where the elk stands longest, and standing still is the whole of what a fungus wants. The right antler is green through and wet with it; the left is still an elk's. The mushrooms come up thickest on the withers, the flat of the back, where you would put your hand on an animal to steady it. Gunnar's map marks the roads between as bad ground and will not say why. He says Sporehorn is no danger where it stops. It is a danger on the way, and he would rather people were not standing in the road when it goes to see about her.

monsters.name: Emberwing
monsters.lore: No bigger than a lantern, it drifts on wings too gaudy for a dragon — then breathes fire that shames its size.
monsters.loreDesc: Wings exact to the last scale, a lantern-sized dragon guessed at, and a jet of flame three times its length.
loreStory: No dragon was ever anywhere to be remembered. What there was, in a hundred countries at once, was the telling of one, and a telling said often enough, to enough people listening, weighs as much here as a life does. So this is not the memory of an animal; it is the memory of an account, and you can see the difference at ten paces. Whoever did most of the remembering had never seen a dragon — no one has — but they had lain in a summer meadow once, watching the irises being worked over close up, and when the account ran out, that is what came to hand. The wings are the best-made thing on it: four of them, violet banded with pink, exact to the last scale. The body is a grey-green guess the size of a lantern. What got looked at came out sharp. What got taken on trust came out approximate.

loreStory.t: Osric

called it a moth with opinions, at a range he has since revised. The fire is the one detail every retelling in every country kept, so it came through whole and unworn, entirely indifferent to the size of the thing carrying it.
Osric

, not yet a year woken and still sure of things, called it a moth with opinions, at a range he has since revised. The tellers do his eyebrows when they tell it, and he sits and lets them, which is most of why the fire likes him. Being wrong about a creature does not make it harmless. It only decides which parts of it are.
Bettany
keeps a page of dragon accounts in
the Chronicle
and cannot get two of the woken to agree on wings, size, colour, or where the hoard was kept. The page carries one sentence every hand has signed. The fire is right.

monsters.name: Sorrel
monsters.lore: A farm horse that outlived its farm. It still waits at the gate each dusk for a hand that never comes.
monsters.loreDesc: A farm horse that outlived its farm. It still waits at the gate each dusk for a hand that never comes.
loreStory: The gate is still standing — two posts and a bar in open grass, the farm gone out from behind it. At dusk the horse comes up the slope, takes its place on the field side facing where the yard was, and waits about an hour to be brought in. The hand it waits for might be at a fire three days' walk from here, no longer able to tell you it ever owned a horse. It might never have woken at all.

loreStory.t: Osric

has been here three years and still counts in living ones, which is why he tried. He took it an apple; it ate the apple out of his hand very politely and went back to standing. He took it a rope; it walked with him most of a field, then turned round without any fuss whatever and walked back. He kept that up the better part of a season, in the hour after the forge was banked, which is not an hour a working man has spare.
Jehanne

watched one evening from the fence and told him to leave the animal be. She would not say why and did not have to; she keeps an appointment of her own at dusk, daily, and has known for years that there is nothing at the other end of it. What she did not tell him was the rest of it — that he had not been trying to move a horse.
Snowmane

has walked people past that gate more than once, at the shoulder of somebody who could not find their way in the dark, and it has never stopped there. It goes with the lost. Whatever else is wrong with the horse at the gate, it knows exactly where it is.

monsters.name: Thornstag
monsters.lore: Corruption walking on too-long legs. Thorned vines drag from its antlers, and flowers die where it browses.
monsters.loreDesc: A thorn-racked stag so dark it reads as a gap in the wood. Violet light in its flank, and nothing regrows behind it.

loreStory.t: Jehanne

plants white bellflowers behind the chapel every spring, because the rite wants them and she has never found the trick of stopping. Thornstag comes in autumn, within a night or two of the same night, and takes the plot down to bare dirt. What it has browsed does not come up again — not that year, not after. She barrows the dead soil out and barrows new soil in, and she does it every time.

loreStory: Inside a lamp's throw of it, which she has been, you get very little. A stag-shaped hole in the dark. A rack too wide for the gap it just came through. A violet seam working in the break of its flank, thin light where ribs ought to be. It has no interest in her whatsoever. She could put a hand on it. She has not.

loreStory.t: Bettany

sat up with her one autumn to get the thing written down and came away with three pages on the stag and nine on the bellflowers, which tells you where the story is. Everybody says fence it. Jehanne has the wood. Jehanne has had the wood four years. She stopped believing a long time ago and could not stop practising; the fires have gone out across half the map; the rota is a courtesy nobody keeps. And that stag has not missed an autumn yet. Ask her plainly and she answers plainly: she would rather be robbed on schedule than left alone.

monsters.name: Amethyrn
monsters.lore: A beast crowned with one great amethyst horn. It headbutts like a landslide and grazes on buried gems.
monsters.loreDesc: A beast crowned with one great amethyst horn. It headbutts like a landslide and grazes on buried gems.
loreStory: Amethyrn never fell and never was anyone. Count instead the men who went into a hill certain — properly certain, the way you are certain of your own hand — that the next foot of rock had something in it, and count how many of them were wrong. Then work out what a few thousand years of that settles into, given nowhere to be and nothing else to do. It got up. It is the size of a cart, plated like a woodlouse, and it is never wrong.

The horn is one piece of amethyst as long as your forearm, and it is not the useful part. What the beast grazes comes back up through its shoulders in clusters, so a bull that has been feeding well is wearing the assay on its own back, and a patient man with a glass can read a whole hill from the next ridge. That is why people follow it. It headbutts like a landslide. That is why they follow it from the next ridge.

loreStory.t: Osric

has spent two years trying to reach a seam before it does and has not managed it once, which he considers unreasonable in a thing that walks slower than he does. He arrived recently enough to still count his age in living years. He is saving — in
gold
, the one substance here that does not drift — and has not yet worked out what for.
Wendell
pointed out, kindly, over a fire, that Osric has all the time there is. Osric said that was the worry.

monsters.name: Prismclaw
monsters.lore: A lynx grown through with crystal. Light bends wrong around it, and its tail-blade sings when it strikes.
monsters.loreDesc: A lynx grown through with crystal. Light bends wrong around it, and its tail-blade sings when it strikes.

loreStory.t: Sigrun

heard one before she saw it and put a hand out to stop the person walking next to her, which is not a thing she does. The tail-blade sings on the strike, one high note, the same note every time. In her trade that sound means a flaw running all the way through, and an edge that is going to let go, and the only open question is on which stroke. She stood in the trees a long while listening to an animal make the noise a bad blade makes, and could not manage to dislike it.

loreStory: The crystal comes up at the shoulders, the hips and the brow, and it is still coming. It sits heaviest on the joints, the worst place on an animal to put weight, so an old one moves like something much older than it is. You can find the rubbing rocks out in the crystal country: a smooth boulder with a scatter of snapped points around the base. That is grooming. It is trying to get something off itself that is itself. The same growth bends the light, so what you see stands a hand's width from where the lynx is, always to the same side, and hunters are taught to strike beside the animal and trust the correction over their own eyes. The ones who cannot make themselves do it come back saying it moved. It did not move. There is no account of one ever moving at that moment.

monsters.name: Nightmule
monsters.lore: A pack beast gone feral in the dark, white-eyed and stubborn. It charges head-first and will not be reasoned with.
monsters.loreDesc: Unharnessed, unloaded, unled — and still keeping to its route. Get in the way and it comes on at a walk.
loreStory: In the life it fell out of, somebody owned it. That is worth knowing, because of what comes off one: a bronze camp knife, hemp rope chewed to a splay, three iron links worn smooth on the inside by years of harness, a roll of coarse grey canvas. One person's kit for going somewhere and stopping for the night, all of it still coming off an animal that is carrying nothing at all.

loreStory.t: It keeps a route. It comes on at a walk, in a line, and the line does not bend around you, because you are standing in a road it was walking before the road went soft.
Wendell
swears the line is the old east road, and for an evening's company he will name you every stop on it — which is one more thing than the animal can do.

loreStory: The load went. The voice up at the front went so long ago there is no name left to put to it. Now and then it halts in open ground, swings both ears forward at nothing whatever, waits to be spoken to, and then walks on.

monsters.name: Sunscale
monsters.lore: A cat armored in noon-light. Its golden scales drink the desert sun and pay it back in blinding flashes.
monsters.loreDesc: A cat armored in noon-light. Its golden scales drink the desert sun and pay it back in blinding flashes.

loreStory.t: More people have followed this cat than any other animal in Nangijala, and every one of them was following something it has not got. The plates look like gold, and gold is
the one thing everybody here agrees about
, so a person who has seen gold is certain about it in a way they are almost never certain about anything. In shade the cat is the colour of ordinary sand. Nothing comes off it. It is a cat.

loreStory: The flash is not a display, it is the entire defence. At noon it turns broadside, the plates take the sun and hand it back, and whoever is behind it loses their eyes for a count of ten, which is all it needs and all it ever uses. Early and late it hides instead, and hides well, because sand is what it actually is. The ones who get close go at dawn and stop expecting gold.

There was a man who followed one for eleven years. He gave up his work for it, walked out of two fires' rotas to do it, and got near enough four times to watch the plates dull over in shadow, which should have ended the business and did not. Asked what he meant to do if he ever caught the animal, he said he had stopped thinking about that part around year three. He was not a fool by then and he was not greedy. He had somewhere to be every morning, in a country where you can wake up and find you have nothing to do for the next four hundred years, and he had decided that was the better half of the bargain.

monsters.name: Ashfiend
monsters.lore: A thin horror with too many eyes and no patience. It strikes with its skull and falls to ash when finished.
monsters.loreDesc: A crowned bone face, two sizes too big for the starved body carrying it. Fights head-first. Goes to ash.
loreStory: It does not walk. It gathers both feet under itself and crosses the ground in bounds, and it takes you crown-first, head down, the hardest thing left on it leading. Nothing that ever hunted for a living fights with its face. And it hurries. Everything empty in the open country has all the time there is; this one moves like something with an errand, and the errand is not its own.

loreStory.t: What comes off one is mostly not its own either. Grey talons of the kind the lit thing sheds. Hooks sized for a big cat's mouth. On
Sigrun
's bench last autumn, out of a head with two red eyes, a whole wet eye, brown.
Osric
, new enough to still ask things out loud, asked what it wanted the eye for. Sigrun tied the bag and put it with the others. Everyone in the room understood the answer except him.
Broken, it folds at the knees and settles, and the settling is ash; the wind has the heap by morning, near
the mouth
as anywhere. It leaves no mask. The face goes with the rest of it — it only goes last.

monsters.name: Balefiend
monsters.lore: Elder kin of the eye-demons, wreathed in flame and swirling dark. Its slam is meant to crush, not to wound.
monsters.loreDesc: Nothing behind the face — four slit eyes burning in black stone, wreathed in dark. Its attack is to fall on you.
loreStory: A face of black stone, four slit eyes lit orange down it, red marks cut above and below them, the whole thing hanging inside a wreath of slow dark that takes fire when it moves. It does not strike. It rises, and it comes down on you with everything it weighs, meaning to crush. And the eyes shut first — all four, a breath before the stone cracks — so whatever was doing the looking is gone before the breaking starts.

loreStory.t: There are two accounts of it and neither has won. One: it is a shell the emptying made when it had nothing left to work with, the outside done beautifully, the inside not attempted. The other: it is one of the masks, left lying too long near
the mouth
, and no longer an object. The crackers prefer the first. The second has a next question in it.
Jehanne

was sent a rubbing of the red marks, on the reasoning that a priestess reads things. She kept it through a winter. In spring she burned it, and told the sender the marks say nothing at all — in the voice she keeps for the prayers she no longer believes. She has not gone east since.

monsters.name: Dunedelver
monsters.lore: It swims through sand the way fish forget water. Only the jagged back-plates betray the tide beneath.
monsters.loreDesc: It swims through sand the way fish forget water. Only the jagged back-plates betray the tide beneath.
loreStory: The dunes are the one ground in this country that keeps nothing. Put a thing under them and the sand hands it back — a week later, a season later, standing on end in a clean hollow with a delver's wake still settling around it. The animal is not looking for your box. There is nothing on the front of it that is looking at anything; it goes through a dune the way something goes through water, on those pale spade-claws, and whatever was down there ends up on top.

loreStory.t: Jehanne

walked three days east of her rota last autumn and buried the bell she calls people to fire with. She tells the story herself, at her own fire, and tells it well: how she could not go on ringing a thing she had stopped believing in, and could not bring herself to break it either, and so put it under a dune and came home lighter than she had walked out. Eleven days. Then a charcoal burner turned up at her door with it, upright and clean and pleased with himself.

loreStory: She rings it every evening now, and the story gets its laugh, and she lets it. What she leaves out is that anyone who has worked that country knows exactly what the dunes do with anything you put in them. She had been out there before. She chose the place.

monsters.name: Voidmaw
monsters.lore: It has no face, only appetite. The ringed mouth opens wider than reason, and the light goes in first.
monsters.loreDesc: It has no face, only appetite. The ringed mouth opens wider than reason, and the light goes in first.
loreStory: Look at the body before you look at the mouth. Four legs, a working shoulder, a tail with a switch in it — the whole frame of something that once grazed and was nervous of dogs. Then the neck ends in rings of teeth around a hole, and there is no face on it anywhere, no part of the head a name could ever have gone into. Violet marks crawl over the hide and give off their own light. Ordinary light goes the other way: hold a torch out toward one and it lights your hand and nothing past it.

There are three words for what a creature is here and not one of them will sit on this. It did not come — nothing that grazed anywhere arrives shaped like that. It was not made; the made are pooled out of what crowds of the dead agree on, and there is no crowd anywhere that agrees on this. And Hollowed means a thing emptied out and left with its outside, the outside being the whole of what the Hollowed keep. This one did not keep a face. The guides file it under Hollowed because a guide has to put a thing somewhere, and the crackers who work that ground will tell you plainly that the guides are guessing.

loreStory.t: Hearn
does not discuss
the mountain

. Everyone knows why and everyone asks anyway. Shown an account of one of these, he broke his own rule for it: not the mountain's work, he said, and then a second sentence nobody had asked for — that the thing under the mountain wants something, and this wants nothing at all, it only opens. He would not go further. His reason was never the Chronicle. People who believe a thing came out of the mountain go east after it, and Hearn has been east once, with company, and does not mean to be why anyone goes again.

monsters.name: Dewling
monsters.lore: A pale meadow blob that balances a dewdrop like a crown — and swings it at whatever wanders too close.
monsters.loreDesc: Round and sand-pale, balancing one bright drop on a stalk. The drop is the weapon and comes round like a flail.
loreStory: The collectors call all the round ones lings, one word for the same business turning up in five kinds of country, and the low country's is pale as dry sand, holding a single bright drop up over itself on a stalk. Of everything a wet field at first light contains, the drop on its stem with the sun inside is the detail everyone keeps exactly; the rest wears down under all that remembering to pale grain, no particular grass, no particular year.

loreStory.t: It swings the drop round like a weight on a line, catching the light as it comes, meaning none of it. The trade's one rule is to work with the sun at your back, because whoever is looking into the flash when the blow lands loses the next few steps of the fight. Flattened, it leaves no body at all, just
something sun-bleached and far too heavy
lying in the pressed grass.
Most mornings one comes partway up the rise toward the fire on
the meadow where everyone wakes
and stops just short of the light, and the fire's oldest joke is that it has come to be met.
Solveig

lets the joke stand. But after a night when the fire sat ready and the meadow stayed empty, she has been seen walking down the wet field to stand beside it a while, and whatever she says there she has never once brought back up the hill.

monsters.name: Sprigling
monsters.lore: A green woodland blob armed with a splinter of oak. Cut it down and it scatters into smaller blobs.
monsters.loreDesc: Green, damp, a shoot coming up out of its head, and a little wooden sword in a fist it does not really have.
loreStory: The wood's ling is green and damp, with a live shoot coming up out of its head. A wood, to nearly everyone who ever remembered one, is a place you went into to take something out of, and the stroke is the part that comes back identical from every rememberer — so it carries a small pale-wood sword out of nowhere in particular and swings it at travellers and passing birds with the same blank willingness. No grudge; there is nothing in it that could hold one.

loreStory.t: Osric

burns charcoal at the wood's edge, and in his first month here — he still said weeks then, as if weeks were load-bearing — one walked its round through his camp every day and swung at him every time. What offended him was not the swinging but the grip. He stopped dodging, took the little fist it does not really have, and set the sword properly in it, the way you set an apprentice's. It struck him anyway. He maintains it struck better.
Broken, it is chips before you can regret it, small green pieces in all directions at once, and what stays behind is
a stone with black grain run through it like sawn timber

. Osric buys those from the woodcutters. His own one still comes through the camp, and he has moved the woodpile out of its road, and he does not say what he will do on the morning the round comes through empty.

monsters.name: Cragback
monsters.lore: A hillside that stood up. Moss and granite shift when it breathes, and climbers swear the mountain growled.
monsters.loreDesc: A hillside that stood up. Moss and granite shift when it breathes, and climbers swear the mountain growled.
loreStory: Every valley had its one hill, and the people in it agreed on that hill's shape the way they agreed on almost nothing else: the same dark line against the same evening, seen from the same doorway, for generation after generation. And every hill of that kind carried the same story — there is a bear up there, do not go up after dark, I mean it. A hundred valleys' worth of that, held identically by everybody who ever lived in sight of one, and it does not stay a hill. The story stood up and brought the hill with it.

loreStory.t: Moving costs it. The seams open green down its legs when it walks and the moss tears along the shoulders, so mostly it declines to, and holds one position for years while people treat it as exactly what it looks like. There was a rota fire on the western rounds kept in its lee for eleven winters — out of the weather, with a wall at your back you could lean on all night. One spring the wall left. The keeper lost the fire twice to the wind before morning and finished the shift anyway, talking to whoever came, in the open, with nothing behind her.
Solveig
has a private word for keepers who do that. She has never once said it to their faces. The wall is somewhere further west now, standing still again, with eleven winters of soot up one flank.

monsters.name: Gnashjaw
monsters.lore: It gnaws boulders to keep its tusks short. When the grinding stops, something softer has wandered close.
monsters.loreDesc: It gnaws boulders to keep its tusks short. When the grinding stops, something softer has wandered close.
loreStory: You find the stones a long time before you find the animal: boulders worn into a shallow saddle, glassy in the dip, three or four of them to a clearing. A teller once copied the grooves off one convinced they were writing, and got as far as ruling out four alphabets before somebody who had actually seen a brute took pity. They are teeth-marks. It grinds its tusks down on rock, all its life, on purpose.

loreStory.t: Ask why an animal would file off its own best weapon and the answer is standing somewhere east, and has been standing there a very long time. A full-grown pair of tusks is a challenge, and there is only one thing in this country worth challenging, and
the old bull
has never lost. So they grind. Every young brute alive spends its whole span wearing itself smaller so it will not have to go and find out.

loreStory: Almost everything else out in that country is at Habit by now, walking a round with the animal long since gone out of it. Not this one. It is entirely present — it is frightened, it is deciding, it grinds — and being present is precisely what the fear costs it. So watch the stones. When the wear on one goes grey and weathered and no fresh cut appears on it for a season, something has been settled out there, and it is a long walk east.

monsters.name: Tuskmaul
monsters.lore: The old bull of the brutes. Whole warbands have broken against shoulders wider than their shield-wall.
monsters.loreDesc: The old bull of the brutes. Whole warbands have broken against shoulders wider than their shield-wall.

loreStory.t: There was an age here with enough people in it, and enough agreement between them, to put a shield-wall in a field and walk it forward in step. Sit with that fact by itself for a moment; it is a larger thing to know about this country's past than anything the animal ever did. Then note that the wall is the part that broke. The bull is out there yet, old past any counting, uninterested. It does not grind its tusks and has not needed to for longer than anyone can account for, and
the young ones
file theirs off rather than come and ask. So no one asks. It moves when it wants the sun.
Hearn

will tell you about that field. Hearn will tell you about it at length: the frost in the ground, the order the flanks went in, the sound a shield-wall makes at the moment it stops being a line and becomes people. He was not there — it was long before him — and he has every yard of it from those who were, and he can hold a fire for a whole evening with it, generous and exact and warm. It is not the story anybody sat down for. They sit down because Hearn went into the mountain with a party and came out of it by himself, and because he once said, of the inside, that it asked politely, and has said nothing since. So he gives them Tuskmaul. He gives them Tuskmaul every single time, and they take it, and they come back next week and take it again.

monsters.name: Quillkin
monsters.lore: A grumpy ball of needles that would rather nap than fight. Corner it and the quills leave first, fast as arrows.
monsters.loreDesc: Still laying in stores for a hand that stopped coming. Crowd this brown handful of spines and the quills stay in.
loreStory: It travels the bottoms of things — walls, hedge-lines, the low sides of paths — on a route that stopped leading anywhere long ago, carrying a fistful of hard glossy kernels it cannot eat and will not be parted from. A hedgehog has no use for a nut. Behind this one was a person who put food out at a certain hour, and an animal that learned to be at the place when they did, and of that whole arrangement the piece that lasted is the being-there. It still arrives at the old hour, to a patch of grass where a doorstep used to be, and waits, and eats nothing, and moves on.

loreStory.t: Wendell

says the wall it keeps to on the old east road was a garden wall, and that he knows whose garden. He is not making it up; the road is his stock in trade, and he sells what he remembers of it for company. So the name this animal has been keeping its appointment with is not gone. It is sitting in an old man by a fire, one evening's listening from being said aloud, and nobody has paid the evening yet.

Crowd it and the quills go in barbed and stay in. Somewhere in the dark there is a black-pelted thing carrying three of them, from a meeting on the low side of a path that neither of them chose or understood. The
white rabbit
keeps an hour of its own, out on open ground. The low country is full of them.

monsters.name: Cinderhowl
monsters.lore: A hound cracked open by its own fire. Embers sift from its seams, and its howl smells of burning.
monsters.loreDesc: A hound cracked open by its own fire. Embers sift from its seams, and its howl smells of burning.
loreStory: A drover on the west road watched one for eight nights from his fire, then went down and walked it into the river. It let him. That is the part he tells badly every time and the part that costs him his sleep: a lean black dog standing chest-deep in cold water while a stranger poured more of it over the split seams along its ribs — steaming, patient, entirely willing — and the orange in the splits never dimmed by a shade. Then it came out, shook itself, and followed him up the bank.

loreStory.t: So he walked to
Sigrun

's door and asked her to release it. She went and looked at it for an afternoon, which is more than she gives most requests, and came back and said no, and gave him the reason in the two flat words of
her trade

. She cracks shapes that are thinning. This one is not thinning. It is holding beautifully — flame at the tail, fire between the ears, embers going out one by one on the ground behind it, every bit of it as steady as the day it arrived. What he wanted done would have been done for him, and she does not do that work for the watcher. She told him to stay off the road after dark. He goes. He reports that it waits for him at the same bend now, at the same distance, burning quietly, and that he talks to it. She has stopped telling him not to.

monsters.name: Rimeshard
monsters.lore: Black rock grown through with living ice. It tears crystal spears from the ground and swings them like clubs.
monsters.loreDesc: Dark rock grown through with ice: a crown, a mouthful, bladed arms, and more torn out of the ground at need.
loreStory: Above the snow line the ground turns crystal and stays that way, and the Rimeshard is what that ground does to a rock that stands in it long enough: dark plates iced through, a crown of blades off the skull, a mouth that is a row of them. When it wants more than it is wearing, it reaches down and tears it out of the ground — up there it and the ground are the same material, and there has never once been a shortage.

So the trade keeps one rule about it, bought dear and given away free: never above the line. Baited downhill onto ground that is merely ground, it spends its crown, then its shoulders, and cannot reach for more, and a patient crew can break the shape by dark. Above the line you are not fighting a creature so much as the ground it stands on, and the ground goes down a long way further than your patience.

loreStory.t: Ask
Hearn
what was under
the mountain

and he goes somewhere behind his own face. Ask him instead about the Rimeshard he passed on the trail down and he will talk all evening: how it marked him, and let him by, and wanted nothing, took nothing, asked him for nothing. He calls it the most restful thing on that whole road. People who work the high ground use the same word, restful — and use it, as a rule, in the season before they come down for good.

monsters.name: Frostling
monsters.lore: A snow-packed blob with a frozen grin. It spits ice spikes, and melts to slush when its winter finally ends.
monsters.loreDesc: Packed snow with two dark eyes, heavier than snow should be. Every spike it throws is grown out of itself.
loreStory: Down in the grass the ground wanders; high under the crystal country nothing has needed correcting in a very long time, and there is hardly anyone left up there to walk on it. Out of ground held that hard comes the high snow's ling: snow pressed into a shape with two dark eyes, far heavier than snow has any business being, and armed entirely out of itself. A spike grows up through its crown and flies, and there is measurably less creature afterwards. It will do that until it cannot.

loreStory.t: Gunnar

goes up each year to check his measurements of the Drift against the one country that never moves, and each year the same one — the eyes set a little crooked; you learn one the way you learn a face — meets him at the last ridge and throws everything it has. He stands out of range and lets it finish. His is the only footfall on that road all year. Whatever it is armed against, he is the whole of what ever arrives.

loreStory: It is smaller each year. He measures it — he measures everything — and keeps the number where he keeps the rest, to himself. They do not shatter at the end; they slump, into slush inside their own footprint, and the wet mark outlasts them by an hour. Gunnar says that the year it does not throw at him, he will retire the route. He says it the way he says most things, so that you cannot tell whether it is a joke.

monsters.name: Winterfang
monsters.lore: Its mane is a crown of ice that never melts. The cold arrives a breath before it does, and stays after.
monsters.loreDesc: Its mane is a crown of ice that never melts. The cold arrives a breath before it does, and stays after.
loreStory: You get the number before you get the animal: the fire wants twice the wood. Then it is at the rim of the light, heavy through the shoulders, a crest of ice grown up out of its neck like a crown hammered on wrong, icicles off the jaw, ice standing out through the claws. It does not come in. It has never once come in.

loreStory.t: Jehanne

had one at her fire for six hours in the black of a winter, with four people to keep warm and the pile going down and the tellings stopped, because you cannot tell a thing properly while you are hauling. A man there wanted it driven off and was right on every practical count. She fed the fire and let it stand, and said afterwards only that a rota does not get to ask who is coming. What she keeps to herself, because it does her no credit as a keeper, is why she thinks it stands there: it is trying to get warm. The cold is the last true thing it has left, and it puts out whatever it walks toward, and cannot learn this, and comes back. She splits a second pile now on the nights the frost arrives early. The man still keeps the rota with her. They have not discussed it once.

monsters.name: Slagling
monsters.lore: A crust of cooled stone with molten rage beneath. It flares white-hot when angered, then melts into slag.
monsters.loreDesc: Under a crust of cooled rock, a fistful of heat going out. To strike, it splits along the seams and flares.
loreStory: A stretch of the black rock is the wrong colour and warm through the boot, and things get up out of ground argued over that hard. What everyone keeps of a fire is not the flame: it is the black skin that forms over a late log with the red still moving underneath. So that is what stood up — the black rock's ling, a fistful of banked heat in a shell of cooled stone, going out from the moment it got up.

It fights by splitting. The seams open, the flare comes all at once, the shell shuts, and there is a little less inside than there was. You cannot hurry one in any way that is not ugly, so the workers up there walk beside it instead and let it spend itself, and by evening it is down to its last light.

loreStory.t: Jehanne
found one guttering above the tree line on a
rota
walk and did what she does at every failing fire on her list: knelt and fed it, stick by stick, half the night, into seams that could not take wood. It went out toward morning anyway. She carries
the ember it left
unsold in her rota coat, and when
Bettany
asked her, for the Chronicle, why she had fed a thing she knew was not a fire, she gave the answer she gives about the evening prayers: the practice was never for the fire.

monsters.name: Emberjaw
monsters.lore: Basks in cooling magma and bites with a mouthful of flame. Its hide stays warm for hours after it falls.
monsters.loreDesc: Basks all day, crusted and cracked open on the light beneath, then gets up breathing fire it never learned.
loreStory: What fell was small: a damp thing the length of a hand, bark-coloured, living under wet wood, no danger to anything and in none itself. What basks on the black rock now stands several times that — hide gone to crust, the crust split along its seams on a steady light, and when the mouth opens, fire comes out. A great many of the dead once put a log on a fire and watched a little creature run out of the flame; every one of them drew the obvious conclusion, and not one went back and checked. When the animal's own account of itself wore thin, their story is what was left holding the shape.

loreStory.t: It spends the day flat on the warm stone, doing just what the story says it should, then gets up and walks a round nothing accounts for and bites whatever is standing in it — and the fire makes the bite the smaller half of the problem.
Jehanne
walks out once a season to look at it. She keeps a rite she stopped believing because people need the fire either way, and she says this creature is her whole argument, standing up and warm.
The coal it finally comes down to
does not cool
. The black rock runs on toward the cave, warmer the whole way, and the creature walks to the edge of that ground and turns back, every time.

monsters.name: Palemaw
monsters.lore: A pale cave-dweller with a jaw built for bone. It bites once, hard, and seldom needs to bite twice.
monsters.loreDesc: Dull olive, pale flat eyes, a gape wider than the skull carrying it. One bite. Rarely two.

loreStory.t: The Chronicle
files it beside
the burning one

because at forty paces they share a silhouette, and there the resemblance ends. Nothing about this animal is lit. It is lichen-olive going grey, the eyes flat, pale and wrong, and the head is mostly jaw — hinged so far back that the gape opens wider than the skull carrying it. It gives no warning at all. One bite, and generally that is the encounter.

What it hunts is the hard things. Bone first — it will spend a night on one marrow bone and leave it knobbed and stained in the open, which is how you know one is working an area — then stone, and gold whenever it finds any, though no one has ever opened one and found gold inside. It works ground nearer the cave than anything else that still has an inside.
Hearn
will guide a cracker as far as the chewed bones and no farther; he waits there facing the mountain, and he does not sit down.
The paws it sheds are never a matching pair: what grows back after a loss comes back approximate, and the next one approximate from the approximation. The hard piece in the jaw is
sea-green, mended through with gold
; what the mend means is an argument for the people who trade it. The animal goes on taking what refuses to go, and has never once looked like it wondered why.

monsters.name: Slagfang
monsters.lore: A wolf quenched in the caldera. Magma veins its black hide, and its bite leaves wounds already cauterized.
monsters.loreDesc: A wolf quenched in the caldera. Magma veins its black hide, and its bite leaves wounds already cauterized.

loreStory.t: Animals wake in the grass too.
Solveig

has met nine wolf-wakings at the meadow fire and has never once got the courtesy to work — you cannot ask an animal its name, and it has no one true thing to give you — so she does the part that carries over. She sits a little way off. She stays until it can stand. Then, every single time, without one exception in nine, it gets up and goes east.

East is the burnt country, and by the time you see one out there it is black-hided with magma standing in the seams and flecks of ember lifting off its back, and it is not travelling alone any more. They arrive one at a time, spaced out by however long each of them took to get here, and they find each other. Solveig has never been east in her life and is certain of one thing about that road: they are not going somewhere. They are going to somebody, and his name is a noise that comes down the slopes at dusk. See
Basalthowl

loreStory: The one last spring was thin-legged and could not stand for most of a day, and she gave it the day, and a man waiting to be met waited. When it finally went it did not look back at her. She says she would think less of it if it had.

monsters.name: Basalthowl
monsters.lore: The pack-sire of the volcanic wolves. When it roars, the mountain answers, and the ash begins to fall.
monsters.loreDesc: The pack-sire of the volcanic wolves. When it roars, the mountain answers, and the ash begins to fall.

loreStory.t: Osric

wanted a fire he would not have to feed. He is a smith, and new — he still counts in living years and lets people correct him — and he had worked out that a man who spends his life on fuel should go and look at ground that is already hot. So he went up to the caldera with a rule and a notebook, and came back with three days of good measurements and one evening he does not offer around.

loreStory: The sire is enormous, black as cooled slag, veined orange through the chest and legs, smoke standing off its shoulders in a plume you can see from the col. At dusk it called, and the pack answered off the slopes one voice at a time, in an order, and Osric counted seven. Then it called once more into a gap in the order and waited. Then again. Six times into the same gap, unhurried, the way you knock at a door you have every reason to think is answered. Then it lay down in the ash.

loreStory.t: He understood the gap. Anyone who has kept anything here does: something up that mountain went
Quiet

, and the count it belonged to has not been corrected and will not be. Osric built his forge on the meadow side instead, where the wood comes in from three hours out and every fire is somebody's labour. He does not tell people the caldera was dangerous. He tells them it was occupied.

monsters.name: Palehusk
monsters.lore: Someone's failed experiment, wearing borrowed skin. It shambles after travellers on limbs that bend wrongly.
monsters.loreDesc: Bare, blotched, hairless and shaped exactly like a person, coming at a walk with one hand open and green.
loreStory: Out on the warm black rock, exactly the shape of a person, bare and blotched and wearing nothing. What tells you at fifty paces is the arms: a walking person's arms swing, and these hang. It follows, and it does not hurry, and when it arrives it does not bite and does not claw. It reaches — one open hand, out and across, green standing in the seams of it, a gesture anybody would recognise. Everyone who has met one says the gesture is the worst part.

It kept things. A bronze locket grown in under the skin of its chest. A pitted silver ring on a finger it was never made for. Grave dirt in the creases. The ones who go through what a broken one leaves are not robbing it, they are reading it, and no name has ever been read off one.

loreStory.t: Hearn
went into
the cave
with the one organised attempt anyone ever made on it, and came out alone, and in all the years since has said exactly one thing about the inside: it asked politely. Last winter at
Solveig
's fire, a cracker fresh off the black rock was describing the open hand. Hearn stood up, and asked which hand, and went out. He has not added anything since.

monsters.name: Diretusk
monsters.lore: A mountain of dark wool and ivory, calm until crowded. One sweep of those tusks clears a road.
monsters.loreDesc: Crowd it and one sweep of ivory clears the road. Otherwise it grazes, wool to the ankles, a herd of one.
loreStory: Nothing else grazing this country comes near it for size: wool to the ankles, a shoulder above a grown person's head, ivory curved out far enough to clear a road. It is not hunting anything and never was. Nearly everything that has ever gone wrong between one of these and a person happened because the person stood too close for too long — the head comes round, one sweep, and the conversation is over.

loreStory.t: Watch the spacing instead. It keeps a gap open on either side of itself, and it halts the way an animal halts when the animal ahead has halted. There is no animal ahead.
Gunnar
, who shares his measurements with no one, still marks the one on his eastern round as a fixed point, the way other maps use hills — the hills out there having proved less dependable.
Bringing one down takes the knees first, then a long settling into the grass, and what is left fits in a closed hand:
a piece of ivory webbed with hairline breaks

. Every one of them is a break it kept walking after — the tusks it sheds are snapped clean at the root by things it never once broke stride for. What the piece lends whoever carries it is exactly what the animal had. Not strength. The habit of continuing while damaged.

monsters.name: Grinmask
monsters.lore: A sliver of living dark behind a grinning mask. Slay it and the shadow is gone; the mask clatters down, still smiling.
monsters.loreDesc: Not a thing that thinned — a thing that was emptied. What falls when it breaks is a mask, and the masks all match.
loreStory: Everything else out there is running on habit — a shape walking its round with the details gone, that will only hurt you for standing in the round. Grinmask stops when you stop and starts when you start. It plays. Crackers who work the eastern ground will take any two of anything else before one of these, because the rest defend themselves and this one has intentions, and the intentions did not come from the shape.

loreStory.t: Break it and the dark is simply not there any more — no struggle, no leaving. What comes down is the mask, and the mask does not thin.
Bettany

drew one for the Chronicle, and two winters later drew another, off a beast broken thirty miles from the first. She laid the new tracing over the old: line onto line, the whole way round. The same face. Smiling, both times — they are always smiling. And the inward side is smooth as a bowl. Not a face something wore. A face something made.
Those two drawings are most of the reason there is an
investigation
at all. Bettany, who has interviewed half the country about the worst day of its life without flinching, keeps both masks face-down in a drawer now, and has stopped drawing them.

monsters.name: Moonpelt
monsters.lore: A wolf the moon keeps. Its silver fur holds the crescent's mark, and its paws never quite touch the frost.
monsters.loreDesc: A wolf the moon keeps. Its silver fur holds the crescent's mark, and its paws never quite touch the frost.

loreStory.t: Wendell

walks between fires after dark, which a man his age has been told not to do, and he has not been alone doing it for eleven winters. Something falls in behind him a little way out and holds thirty paces — exactly thirty, over broken ground and through water — and comes as far as the edge of the light and no farther. Silver, a blue crescent set in the fur of the brow, seams of cold colour down the shoulders. He calls it his escort and means it.

loreStory: Look at the frost under it. There is a hand's width of nothing there, no print in the rime, and after a night in new snow the road behind Wendell shows one set of boots. He knows what that is. It has let go of the ground the way you let go of a name, and what goes after the ground goes fast.

So he talks to it the whole way. Not chatter — proper tellings: the east road when it was still walked, his sister's stubbornness, the winter the wells went strange. Others say a telling wants somebody listening and an animal is not somebody. Wendell answers that it walks when he talks and stops when he stops, and that this will have to do, and that he could not tell you which of the two of them is holding the other up anyway. Both of them are still here. He considers the argument closed.

monsters.name: Mirewart
monsters.lore: Fattened on swamp-magic and far too clever. Novices laugh at it once, then learn to respect the slam.
monsters.loreDesc: A green weight in the shallows, in no hurry to move, and the first live thing this country shows its newly woken.

loreStory.t: Animals fall into this country too, and no one meets them; there is nothing useful anyone can say to a frog. This one has held the shallows at the low end of the meadow since before the roads were where they are, working the only trade it knows: sit where the flies come, hold still, be patient. The low wet ground is where
the newly woken

drift while they still cannot say their own names, so the first live thing this world shows a great many people is a green weight with a hard yellow eye on each side of its head, looking back and not getting up.
Wendell

woke when the east road was still safe and could not find his name for three days, and got it back sitting in that mud, saying pieces of it to the frog — because you can say a name wrong to a frog, and say it wrong again, and it asks nothing back. He has traded the story for company at fires ever since. Last spring
Osric
came up from those same shallows with wet boots and the same story, and Wendell will not hear a word about it being a different frog.
It is also, often, the first thing the frightened ones break: it is close, it is slow, it does not run. The small warm stone it leaves
sets quietly to work
closing the knuckles of the very hand that did it. So Wendell gives every one of the newly woken he can catch the same advice: go down and tell the frog your name. It will not care. That is the gift.

monsters.name: Glowbone
monsters.lore: Its bones burn through split hide, lighting the woods it hunts. You see the glow long before the claws.
monsters.loreDesc: Dark hide split at the shoulders and spine, lit bone standing up through it. You see one coming a long way off.

loreStory.t: On all fours, hunched, arms too long and ending in fingers, the hide split along the shoulders and spine with lit bone standing up through the splits. The keepers of the old eastern circuit called it the last mercy near
the mouth
: the one thing out there that cannot cross a black wood without announcing itself.
Wendell
walked that circuit young, and will still trade you the saying, along with everything else he remembers of the east, for an evening's company.
Gunnar

will not sit through that particular evening any more. Gunnar watched one hunt. The light stood up out of its ribs at a creature that had lived in the dark long enough to give up on light, and the creature stayed exactly where it was, blind, while the long arm arrived. The light is not leaking, and it was never a mercy. It is the part that does the work.

Breaking one goes wrong in a particular way: it comes apart at the neck, the lit head leaves first, and the rest stands up on its hands a moment longer — the part everyone reaches in the telling and then skips. The light does not go down with it.
The piece it leaves
is still burning, and not one hour of all that burning, out in all that dark, was ever lit for anybody.

monsters.name: Magmane
monsters.lore: A lion poured from the volcano's throat. Its obsidian mane cools black; its roar glows through the cracks.
monsters.loreDesc: A lion poured from the volcano's throat. Its obsidian mane cools black; its roar glows through the cracks.
loreStory: Strike the light, not the dark. That is the whole of what the trade knows about it, and it is a worse rule than it sounds. Cold, the glass is armour: a spear takes a chip out of the mane, skates off, and the animal does not appear to notice it has been hit. The cracks only open when it is roused, so the one part of it that can be worked is the part that is not there until it has decided about you. Finding one is the easy half. Look for a scatter of boulders with nothing growing on any of them.

loreStory.t: Osric

went up to look on purpose. He still counts in living years, and he had spent all of them at a forge in a country with no mountains in it. He got within thirty feet, sat down on the scree and watched it sleep the afternoon out, black and cold and breathing about once a minute. What he wanted was the heat. He asked about it afterwards, carefully, the way a new smith asks a question he suspects is stupid, and got the trade's answer: it is the hottest thing in the country and the only fire in it you cannot sit at, and you cannot tell it anything either. He has been up three times since. A man arrived here with a working life still in his hands, in a place that needs nothing made, and the one great heat within reach of him is no use to anybody. He has stopped mentioning it at the fire.

monsters.name: Blightcur
monsters.lore: Sickness on four legs. It survived what it carries, which is more than those it visits can say.
monsters.loreDesc: Sickness on four legs. All it wants is to sit near somebody, and everything already thinning pays for it.
loreStory: It has never been known to go for anyone. It comes at a walk with its head low, olive and gaunt, spine and ribs up under a hide gone patchy and pale-knotted at the shoulders, and it stops at about twenty paces and lies down and stays. The eyes are the only bright thing on it. That is the entire behaviour. It would like to be near somebody.

A bright shape takes nothing from it worse than a foul week and a taste of old metal behind the teeth. What matters is what it does at the far end of the road. Sit an already-thinning man three nights inside that twenty paces and he loses ground he will not get back — Faded to Habit inside a season, in the two cases anyone wrote down, with no wound on him and no fight and nothing to point at. It cannot break you. It can only cost you what you had left.

loreStory.t: Gunnar

keeps most of what he measures to himself. Not this. He plots its line a week ahead and walks the fires along it to tell the old ones to move for a season, and he gives that one away free and gives it away furious, because the fire that has to move is always the one with somebody in it who cannot walk far. Then it follows them — not hunting, nothing that clean. It follows whoever sat still long enough to be near. Drive it off and it goes twenty paces and lies down again.

monsters.name: Bergclaw
monsters.lore: Carved by the glacier and jealous of it. Its frozen tusks crack shields the way spring cracks river ice.
monsters.loreDesc: It woke in warm grass with a life of sea ice behind it, and grew its own back. The tusks are that same ice.
loreStory: It woke where everything wakes: in the meadow grass, in warm air, within sight of the house and the fire, with a whole life of frozen sea behind it and no ice anywhere it could see. There is a courtesy for that hour — you sit with the newly woken and ask their name and one true thing. Nobody has worked out how to do that for something with no name to give. It stood up on its own and went north, and kept going north, and there is nothing that far north but weather.

The ice came afterwards, and it came out of the bear. The crystals stand up through the coat at the shoulders and will not melt — not in rain, not in a warm month, not held in a hand. The tusks are the same stuff, grown down past a jaw with no business growing anything. It carries its own winter because there was not one here to be had.

loreStory.t: And it walks toward fires. That is the whole trouble with it: a bear goes by smell and warmth, and a tended fire is the warmest, best-smelling thing this country has. So every so often the cold arrives before the animal does, and a keeper looks up to find a great pale shape sitting just outside the light, not coming nearer, not going.
Jehanne

has had one sit out three of her nights this year. She has taken to setting something down past the stones before she starts, which is in no rota she was ever given. She will not call it a prayer. She says so quickly, more than once, and she has not missed a night since it started coming.

monsters.name: Gnarloak
monsters.lore: Roots that dreamed of being a bear. It sleeps for whole seasons, and wakes furious at whatever an axe is.
monsters.loreDesc: Roots that dreamed of being a bear. It sleeps for whole seasons, and wakes furious at whatever an axe is.
loreStory: Nobody ever felled this one, because it was never a tree. It is built out of the other half of an extremely ordinary memory: everyone who ever swung an axe remembers the tree going over. The crack, the hinge, the long lean, the ground coming up. Hundreds of thousands of people holding that same half-minute — and the part they kept was never their own arms. It was the tree. Enough of that pooled under one canopy and it gets up, wearing a crown of moss and mushrooms it never grew, having gone over its whole life and never once held a handle.

loreStory.t: It sleeps whole seasons, deep enough that people who work a wood will tell you exactly where it lies and walk over it without lowering their voices. You may carry anything you like across that ground.
Osric

carried a new axe, hafted that morning, because he is not long woken and still counts in living years, and where he came from an axe on your shoulder meant work and nothing else. He does not remember the afternoon. He came back together at the fire that evening, short one afternoon and one good haft.

loreStory: He still makes them; people need firewood, and a smith with opinions about axes is no use to anyone. But he asks now, out loud, before taking the work: what is this one for. And he goes around the north wood rather than through, which costs him an hour he does not mention. The wood has no opinion about Osric at all. It has one about the axe.

monsters.name: Runemane
monsters.lore: A guardian left running after its temple fell. The cyan runes still burn with orders no one can rescind.
monsters.loreDesc: A guardian left running after its temple fell. The cyan runes still burn with orders no one can rescind.
loreStory: The temple is not there. That is the first thing to get straight about the field it walks: no wall, no step, no floor, only long grass, a lion cut from a paler stone than any hill within a day of it, and a square. The runes down its chest and legs still hold their light. Whatever they said, they were an instruction, and the person who could have taken it back has been out of the world long enough that the building went with him.

loreStory.t: Gunnar

measures ground for a living, so he spent four days at a careful distance writing down where it turned. What he has now is a floor plan. Twenty-two paces by nine, a gap in one long side, a smaller square inside that the lion walks around rather than through. A building nobody remembers, on a single sheet, with no name to put at the top of it.
Wendell

went that road while the roof was still on. Ask him and he will give you the animal at the door in detail, the size of it, the colour of the light, how it never turned its head, and not one thing about the room behind. He is old enough to be honest about what that means. The hall went the way unspoken things go and the guard did not, because the guard is the part people tell each other about. It still will not cross the line where the wall stood. It goes round to the gap and comes in the way you are supposed to.

monsters.name: Duskfang
monsters.lore: A shadow-furred hunter out of an older age. It runs down what it wants and ends the argument in one bite.
monsters.loreDesc: A hunter left over from an age this country stopped telling, black-furred, amber-eyed, built for one rush.
loreStory: The fangs are longer than the mouth can shut over, so the jaw has to open the whole way before they are any use, and by then you are out of choices. It lies in open grass for hours doing nothing, calm the way a cat is calm — not calm at all, a decision that has not been taken yet. Then the whole animal happens at once. It was built for one rush, and there is no account anywhere of a second.

It came down out of an age so far back that everyone who woke remembering it has since thinned or gone on, so it never comes up at the fires. Untold things go in order: the plain went first, then the weather on the plain, then the others of its kind, strung out along the line of a hunt. What is left in the grass is the last hundred yards of one.

loreStory.t: Bettany

asked at four fires for one story about it and got blank looks, which frightened her more than the animal did. So she walked out, sat a careful distance from one for a day, and wrote what she saw into
the Chronicle
— noting in the margin that being looked at is not the same as being told about. It is the only entry in her book with no teller behind it.

monsters.name: Gloompard
monsters.lore: Count its violet eyes and you have already lost it. The smoke it trails is the only warning anyone gets.
monsters.loreDesc: Count its violet eyes and you have already lost it. The smoke it trails is the only warning anyone gets.
loreStory: Count the eyes. There are four, two low and wide and two smaller up on the brow, and by the time you have counted them you are inside the distance it needs — the joke every teller makes, and the reason the count is the first thing said about it. What the tellers leave out is that it used to have two. The oldest heads at the black-wood fires learned it with two, and will admit as much if you are patient.

Nothing about a cat in the dark survives being told except eyes. Ask anyone who has met one what they saw and you get eyes, then a smell, then how fast it was, in that order, every time. That is most of what this one is now: the parts that get told, kept hard, the rest let go. The smoke off its back is the same business, the smear of dark that follows anything you only half saw. It has been thinning for centuries and thickening exactly where people hold it, and the two have met in the middle to make something that is nearly all warning and hardly any animal.

loreStory.t: Jehanne

has had the argument three times and never lost it. The proposal is always identical: stop telling it. Leave it out of the round, let it go the rest of the way, and the black wood is quiet inside a generation. She keeps a rota for a faith she stopped believing in years ago and she will not do this. A fire that decides what it is prepared to remember, she said once and has not said since, has stopped being a fire and become a committee. So the telling goes on, and the animal keeps getting better at being one.

monsters.name: Frostwraith
monsters.lore: Gaunt, winged and starving in the drifts. Its ice-claws leave frost-burned wounds that are slow to close.
monsters.loreDesc: Gaunt, four-horned, snow to the claws. The wings never beat. Two colours on it are wrong, and both are hot.
loreStory: Snow-coloured from the crest to the claws, so the first thing anybody sees of one is its eyes. It comes on its feet, wings held open and never once beaten, and makes no sound at all on the snow, and it does not stop hunting, because there is almost nothing up there to catch and nothing in it that could ever be full. What the claws open does not close; the cold moves into the wound and settles.

loreStory.t: The trouble is not what it is. The trouble is where it is. The high snow lies a great many days uphill, on the far side of the massif from
the mouth
, over country more of the dead have agreed on, for longer, than any other ground in the world. People called it safe on exactly that reasoning: too well remembered to lose.
Gunnar

came down off that country in spring with his survey unfinished, which no one had known him to do. He had found talon sockets in the drift, ragged, in matched sets, a whole season's line of them, and he had taken a bearing along the line. The sockets are on his map now. The bearing he keeps where he keeps most of what the ground has been doing lately — to himself — and the people who trust Gunnar's silences have started going the long way west.

monsters.name: Nightmare
monsters.lore: It gallops where sleep is thin. Pale flames mark its passing, and by morning no one recalls their dreams.
monsters.loreDesc: It gallops where sleep is thin. Pale flames mark its passing, and by morning no one recalls their dreams.
loreStory: The pale fire is only at the ends of it — hooves, mane, tail, the parts that move most. The rest is a black horse in good condition with a bright, interested eye that looks straight back at you. It is not remotely quiet about its work, either. Half the accounts begin with somebody sitting up in the grass to watch it go by.

What it costs is one night's dreaming. Everybody within earshot wakes rested and cheerful with a clean gap where the night was, and no way to miss what they cannot remember having had. That is not nothing. A great many of the dead only ever see their people in dreams — the ones who never came, the ones they will not name at a fire because saying it aloud is more than they can manage. A woman on the north circuit had been seeing her mother most nights for two hundred years. She is quite cheerful now.

loreStory.t: Gunnar
has been tracking where it runs for six years, because tracking what the country is quietly losing is what he does.
Bettany
has a page open for it in
the Chronicle

and it is a short page. He has given her the dates, the ground, the weather and the hour, and not the one thing she keeps asking for, which is which way it goes. Twice she has asked. Twice he has talked about something else until she stopped. She wrote that down too, in the margin, because it is the second thing he will not tell her.

monsters.name: Mosscairn
monsters.lore: Moss-clad boulders bound by old earth-magic. It rips the ground open with one fist; the head topples first.
monsters.loreDesc: A cairn that got up. Moss on every weathered face, a flat head low in the shoulders, one fist that opens ground.
loreStory: Every field anybody ever worked was cleared first, and every cleared field kept its heap: rounded brown stones at the edge of the ground, added to a little each season, walked around for a lifetime, never once taken from. Enough of that, in enough fields, and one of the heaps has a face in it. Add to it and welcome — travellers still set a stone on its shoulder in passing, the way you would on any cairn, and it takes no notice. Take from it, even one stone, and you meet the fist. A heap only ever grew. Being taken from is the thing that was never done to it.

loreStory.t: People chance the fist anyway, because in the fall of a broken one there is sometimes raw
gold
, and a pocket of gold buys a great deal of nerve.
Wendell

refuses to call that a fair trade. On the old east road there is a Mosscairn carrying, third down from the crown, a flat grey stone he set there himself — one trip a year, forty years of trips, back when the road was safe and he still walked it. His waymark is out there yet, riding the shoulder of a thing that walks a road he no longer dares. Bring him word of where it stands now and he will sit you down at his fire until you have heard the whole road, mile by mile, the way it was.

monsters.name: Magmashell
monsters.lore: Ancient, grumpy, and full of banked fire. The cracks in its shell glow brighter the angrier it gets.
monsters.loreDesc: Hot stone in a tortoise's shape, orange banked in every seam. Still keeping a crossing that stopped being used.
loreStory: Of the ways over the gorge, one is no longer taken. The path up to it went elsewhere in a Turn, the walk round came out shorter than the climb, and the crossing has carried nothing but weather since. The tortoise on it was never posted there. For a long stretch of years, everyone who described a high crossing also described what waits on one — something old, something slow, something you do not argue with — and when this crossing emptied, all that describing had nowhere left to live. It came up out of the ground into the gap and took the post.

There is a toll, and the toll is a pause. Stop at the edge of its span, stand still for the length of a slow breath, and it swings its bulk aside and lets you over. Try to save the breath and the seams come up bright from tail to skull, and by then it is generally too late to have wanted the other route.

loreStory.t: Gunnar
pays the pause twice a year, in both directions, the only regular the crossing has left. A crossing that carries no one, he says, goes in the end
the way of anything untold

, and a man who maps the Drift wants one fixed thing to measure from. That is what he says. His measurements he keeps to himself, and the walk round, people have begun to notice, comes out a little longer every year.

monsters.name: Voltshell
monsters.lore: Storms nest in the crystals on its shell. It crosses a valley in a lifetime, thunder rolling in its wake.
monsters.loreDesc: Storms nest in the crystals on its shell. It crosses a valley in a lifetime, thunder rolling in its wake.

loreStory.t: No one in that valley gives a distance in miles. They say: as far as the shellback, or a day past it, or it was at the alders when I woke and it is at the beck now, so work it out yourself. It walks one line at the pace of a shadow coming off a wall and has never once turned aside. The crystals are the weather's business rather than its own — sit against the shell through a storm and you feel them go off through the stone, and the animal does not change its footing. It is not the
one on the gorge crossing
, which was never anywhere and never an animal. This one woke here like everybody, out of some country that had real weather in it.

loreStory: The woman who kept the fire at the head of that valley walked out to it every eighth day, for a stretch of years she had long stopped counting, and talked the whole way round it. The rota. Who had come. Who was going soft. What the wind was doing to the alders. A telling wants somebody listening, and there was no one else left on that road, and she had decided the shellback would do — she said so to anyone who raised it, in the tone of a person who has already had the argument with herself and won it.

loreStory.t: She went
Quiet

out there, in the ordinary way, slowly. The ground where the shellback lies up is still the sharpest ground in the valley: grass with edges on it, stones that have not shifted through a Turn, while the far end of the same road has gone the colour of an idea. The tortoise has made perhaps two fields since. It did not stop for her and it does not carry one word she said. What holds that ground is not the tortoise. It is four hundred years of somebody standing next to it, talking.

monsters.name: Stormcrown
monsters.lore: Lightning courts its antlers. It stands on the high fells in the worst weather, daring the sky to try.
monsters.loreDesc: Lightning courts its antlers. It stands on the high fells in the worst weather, daring the sky to try.
loreStory: Go up the high fells in filthy weather and there it is, planted where the ground runs out, facing down into the wind with the summit at its back. Lightning comes to the antlers the way pigeons come to a sill. It does not shy and it does not lie down, and the white of its eye is the brightest thing on the mountain. Whatever it is doing it has been doing since before anyone thought to count, and there is nobody in there to leave off doing it.

A woman climbs up to stand near it. Different weather, same stag, five or six times a year. Standing near it in a storm is how you get broken — the bolt takes the antlers or it takes you — and what is left of you re-forms beside the nearest tended fire some hours later, short a little of what you were thinking.

loreStory.t: The nearest tended fire is
Solveig

's, out on the meadow, a long walk from those fells, and the walk is the point: she gets the whole way back to notice what she has put down. Solveig has met her nine times. She does the courtesy every time — sits with her, tells her what has happened to her, asks her name and one true thing. The name still comes. The one true thing is shorter each time. Solveig asked her once what she goes up there for. She said: because he does not flinch, and I want to see how it is done.

monsters.name: Mireback
monsters.lore: A bear the swamp claimed and gave back. Mushrooms fruit on its shoulders; its jaw closes like a bog-gate.
monsters.loreDesc: A bear the swamp claimed and gave back. Mushrooms fruit on its shoulders; its jaw closes like a bog-gate.
loreStory: It did not go into the swamp. The swamp arrived. This was a wood bear on wood-bear ground, doing the ordinary work of being one, and then the land re-remembered itself around it across a few slow years — and now the trail it knows is four feet under, and the trees it knows are stumps standing in water, and it is still walking the round. Out at the same bank. Up a slope that is not there any more. Three long pauses at nothing in particular. Back.

loreStory.t: You can read how long from its shoulders, because moss does not take on an animal that moves, and the red-caps come in after the moss, in tiers, and only where a thing has stood still through a great deal of wet.
Gunnar

dates them the way other people date weather. He keeps his measurements to himself as a rule and gives this one away free, because the animal is not lost and is not looking for anything, and that makes it worse to meet: it is not wandering across your path, you are standing in the middle of its wood. The jaw comes down like a gate dropping, with no warning in it at all, and from where the bear is you were never anywhere but underfoot.

monsters.name: Bogstalker
monsters.lore: Yellow eyes just above the waterline, algae drifting where it waits. The swamp's stillness is a hunting pose.
monsters.loreDesc: Yellow eyes just above the waterline, algae drifting where it waits. The swamp's stillness is a hunting pose.

loreStory.t: Fen-walkers carry a coat they never wear. It goes rolled on the end of a pole, about the size and shape of a person crouching, and when the water moves wrong you throw it as far as you can and walk the other way. It works four times in five, the best odds out there, and it works because of what is left of this animal. Carry the pole anyway when you cross:
the other cat
in that fen does not hide and will not be fooled by a coat.

loreStory: It is far along. What thins out of a hunting cat goes in an order, and the order is the country first, then the prey, then the difference between the prey and anything else with roughly that outline. What it still holds, perfectly, is one silhouette and the conviction that the silhouette is food. It has gone at a barrow with a sack on it, at a bundled coat, and at its own reflection in flat water, which is the one people find hard to watch.

The low ford was kept for years by a woman who fed it. Not sentiment; she had worked out that a fed one lies up and a hungry one comes to the causeway, and she would rather buy the crossing than defend it. She thinned in her turn and went Quiet, and the cat is still on that stretch, and there is still meat on the flat stone by the water most weeks. The walkers took the job over between them. Not one of them can tell you her name.

monsters.name: Mireglare
monsters.lore: Its stare bores through the fen-mist and burns. Hunters who meet those still eyes are found lit from within.
